# Page blocks

From [the component index](../components.md). A prop with `?` is optional, and `= x` is its default. An indented line is the shape of a value the prop takes. In the examples, `children`, `transactions`, the icons and the handlers stand for the screen's own content, data and state.

## PageHeader

```tsx
import { PageHeader } from "@tuja/ui/components/page-header";
```

The top of every page: eyebrow, the `<h1>`, a description and the page's own actions.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<header>`):

- `title: ReactNode` — The page's title, rendered as its `<h1>`.
- `description?: ReactNode` — One or two sentences under the title that say what the page is for, in muted text.
- `eyebrow?: ReactNode` — A short muted line above the title, such as a date or where the page sits.
- `actions?: ReactNode` — The page's own actions, such as an "Add" button or a month switcher, at the end of the header.

Example:

```tsx
function PageHeaderExample() {
  return (
    <PageHeader
      eyebrow="Finance · Household"
      title="Transactions"
      description="Review this month and fix what the bank sync could not categorise."
      actions={
        <Button look="primary" size="sm" icon={<PlusIcon weight="bold" />}>
          Add transaction
        </Button>
      }
    />
  );
}
```

## StatGroup, Stat

```tsx
import { StatGroup } from "@tuja/ui/components/stat-group";
import { Stat } from "@tuja/ui/components/stat";
```

Key figures in a row, such as spent, income and net, each on a card or plain inside one.

`Stat` and `StatGroup` both import from `@tuja/ui/components/stat` too.

### StatGroup

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The stats, each a `Stat`.
- `look?: "cards" | "plain" = "cards"` — `cards` puts each stat on a card of its own.

### Stat

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<dl>`):

- `label: ReactNode` — What the figure counts, in small muted text above it, such as "Spent".
- `value: ReactNode` — The figure itself, such as "£2,184.20": the largest text of the stat, in figures of one width.
- `detail?: ReactNode` — A muted line under the figure that gives it a context, such as "£312 less than October".
- `icon?: ReactNode` — A small icon at the end of the label's line.
- `intent?: "default" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info" = "default"` — Colours the figure by what it means: `success` for a good result such as money in, `danger` for a loss or a fault, `warning` for something that needs attention, `info` for a neutral note.

Example:

```tsx
function StatGroupExample() {
  return (
    <StatGroup>
      <Stat
        label="Spent"
        value="£2,184.20"
        detail="£312 less than October"
        icon={<ArrowDownRightIcon weight="bold" />}
      />
      <Stat label="Net" value="+£2,065.80" intent="success" />
      <Stat label="Needs a category" value="3" intent="warning" />
    </StatGroup>
  );
}
```

## SettingList, SettingRow

```tsx
import { SettingList } from "@tuja/ui/components/setting-list";
import { SettingRow } from "@tuja/ui/components/setting-row";
```

A settings page: one row per setting, its name and description at the start and one control at the end.

### SettingList

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The rows, each a `SettingRow`.

### SettingRow

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `children?: ReactNode` — Content that depends on the setting, under the name and lined up with it, such as the field for a folder name under the switch that turns the folder on.
- `label: ReactNode` — The setting's name, at the start of the row.
- `description?: ReactNode` — What the setting changes, in muted text under the name.
- `control?: ReactNode` — The one control at the end of the row, such as a `Switch` or a `Select` without a `label`, or a `Button`.

Example:

```tsx
function SettingListExample() {
  const [enabled, setEnabled] = useState(true);
  return (
    <Card>
      <SettingList>
        <SettingRow
          label="Send a morning report"
          description="Get the report by email each day."
          control={
            <Switch
              value={enabled ? "on" : "off"}
              onChange={(next) => {
                setEnabled(next === "on");
              }}
            />
          }
        />
        <SettingRow
          label="Delivery time"
          control={
            <Select
              size="sm"
              defaultValue="07:30"
              options={[{ value: "07:30", label: "07:30" }]}
            />
          }
        />
      </SettingList>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## FormFooter

```tsx
import { FormFooter } from "@tuja/ui/components/form-footer";
```

The Cancel and Save buttons at the end of a form, optionally sticky.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The form's actions, such as a ghost "Cancel" and a primary "Save changes", in reading order.
- `divider?: boolean = false` — Draws a line above the actions, to set them apart from the last field.
- `sticky?: boolean = false` — Keeps the actions in view at the bottom of the screen, or of the scrolling column, while the form scrolls under them, and lets them go at the end of the form.

Example:

```tsx
function FormFooterExample() {
  return (
    <form css={stack.group}>
      <TextField label="Folder name" defaultValue="Finance/Receipts" />
      <FormFooter sticky>
        <Button look="ghost">Cancel</Button>
        <Button look="primary" type="submit">
          Save changes
        </Button>
      </FormFooter>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## EmptyState

```tsx
import { EmptyState } from "@tuja/ui/components/empty-state";
```

What a list, card or page shows when it has nothing yet, with the action that fills it.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `icon?: ReactNode` — An icon on a soft plate above the title, such as the icon of what is missing.
- `title: ReactNode` — What is missing, in a few words, such as "No transactions yet".
- `description?: ReactNode` — One or two sentences under the title: why the place is empty, or what fills it.
- `action?: ReactNode` — The action that fills the place, such as a `Button` "Add a transaction", under the text.
- `level?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3` — The heading rank of the title, for the outline of the page.

Example:

```tsx
function EmptyStateExample() {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      icon={<ListChecksIcon weight="bold" />}
      title="No rules yet"
      description="Make a rule from any transaction, and the bank sync files the next one for you."
      action={
        <Button look="outline" size="sm" icon={<PlusIcon weight="bold" />}>
          Add a rule
        </Button>
      }
    />
  );
}
```

## Columns

```tsx
import { Columns } from "@tuja/ui/components/columns";
```

Two or three columns side by side, such as a main column and an aside, that stack on a narrow box.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The columns, in reading order: each child is one column.
- `ratio?: "1:1" | "2:1" | "1:2" | "3:1" | "1:3" | "1:1:1" = "1:1"` — How the width is shared, first column first: `"2:1"` gives the main column two thirds and an aside one third.
- `gap?: "item" | "group" = "group"` — The space between the columns, and between them where they stack.

Example:

```tsx
function ColumnsExample() {
  return (
    <Columns ratio="2:1">
      <Card>{children}</Card>
      <div css={stack.group}>
        <Card>{children}</Card>
        <Card>{children}</Card>
      </div>
    </Columns>
  );
}
```
